inputs.name: Finite extensions of complete discretely valued fields
inputs.accepted_statement: A finite extension of Q_l carries the unique extended absolute value, is complete, and has discrete valuation. The rank-d integral lattice and exact quotient cardinality are proved in LK1/LK4.
inputs.author: J. S. Milne
inputs.title: Algebraic Number Theory
inputs.theorem_reference: Theorem 7.38; the degree/ramification interpretation is also Corollary 7.42.
inputs.specialization: Apply to the original finite K subset PadicAlgCl(l), with the restricted unique norm; no new field model or global completion is selected.

inputs.name: Finite local cohomology, local Tate duality and the local invariant
inputs.accepted_statement: For a characteristic-zero nonarchimedean local field, finite discrete continuous Galois modules have finite cohomology, vanish in degree >=3, and cup product with their multiplicative Tate dual gives perfect finite duality under the usual local Brauer invariant. Kummer and Hilbert 90 identify H2(mu_m) with Br(K)[m].
inputs.author: J. S. Milne
inputs.title: Arithmetic Duality Theorems
inputs.theorem_reference: I Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.3, together with the Kummer computation in the proof of Theorem 2.1 and the local class formation invariant of I 1.6(b).
inputs.errata_checked: 2026-11-22; the cited correction concerning higher local fields is outside this finite extension of Q_l case.
inputs.specialization: R=Z/l^r, any finite nonfree R-module. LK1 identifies original cochains; LK3 writes the exact cyclotomic dual, H2 target, cochain cups and finite bidual argument, including the flipped H1 map.

inputs.name: Finite local Euler-Poincare formula
inputs.accepted_statement: For a finite discrete G_K module A of order q invertible in the local field K, |H0||H2|/|H1| = |O_K/q O_K|^(-1).
inputs.author: J. S. Milne
inputs.title: Arithmetic Duality Theorems
inputs.specialization: K has residue characteristic l and [K:Q_l]=d. LK4 computes |O_K/q O_K|=q^d for q=|M|, without assuming M free. It includes l=2 and the zero module.

not_assumed: Freeness of the finite coefficient module
An infinite-level Selmer duality or global integral H2 comparison
